questions.stem: Per this page, what does the unicode escape `\u000A` do inside a text block's content line?

options.text: It turns into a newline in the last step, the same way that \n does
options.says: The page says unicode escapes are handled before the text block is parsed at all, not in the escape step where \n is handled.

options.text: It stops the compile, since a text block may not hold unicode escapes
options.says: The page says such a text block compiles; it only warns that the result is surprising.

options.text: It breaks the source line early, and the rest starts a line at column 0
options.says: The page says the lexer turns it into a real line break, so the text after it is a new content line at column 0, which changes the incidental whitespace.

questions.stem: Per this page, which two escape sequences were introduced specifically for text blocks?

options.text: \""" for the delimiter and \' for a single quote
options.says: The page lists \" and \' among the traditional escapes that text blocks keep supporting, not among the new ones.

options.text: \s for a space and \ at the end of a line
options.says: The page names \s, which keeps trailing whitespace, and the line-ending \, which suppresses the line break, as the two new escapes.

options.text: \u for unicode and \0 for the null character
options.says: The page treats unicode escapes as handled by the lexer and \0 as a traditional escape that works in text blocks too.
